Black Myth: Wukong — игра, которая кажется легендой, ставшей живой. С первых минут ощущается, что это не просто игра, а художественное произведение, выточенное с любовью и уважением к китайской мифологии. Визуал ошеломляет: каждый кадр — как картина, каждая локация — это миф, оживший на экране. Особенно впечатляют дизайны чудовищ и духов: от зловещих до величественных, они не просто враги, а персонажи со своей историей и характером. ?? Геймплей — это чистый кайф. Боевая система динамична, тактична и глубокая. Ты не просто машешь посохом, ты — Сунь Укун, Великий Мудрец Равный Небесам. Возможность превращаться в разных существ — не только геймплейная фишка, но и шикарная реализация духа "Путешествия на Запад". Музыка и озвучка — на высоте. Саундтрек одновременно эпичный и медитативный, идеально дополняет атмосферу. Каждое слово и звук будто бы вплетены в ткань древнего эпоса. Это игра, которую не просто проходишь — ею живёшь. Она вызывает и восторг, и трепет, и искреннюю благодарность за то, что такие проекты существуют. Game Science создали не просто экшен — они сотворили культурный мост между Западом и Востоком, между мифом и игрой. Оценка: 10 из 10. Легенда в каждый пиксель. |Black Myth: Wukong is a game that feels like a legend come to life. From the first minutes, you can feel that this is not just a game, but a work of art, crafted with love and respect for Chinese mythology. The visuals are stunning: every frame is like a painting, every location is a myth brought to life on the screen. The designs of monsters and spirits are especially impressive: from sinister to majestic, they are not just enemies, but characters with their own history and character. ?? The gameplay is pure joy. The combat system is dynamic, tactical and deep. You are not just waving a staff, you are Sun Wukong, the Great Sage Equal to Heaven. The ability to transform into different creatures is not only a gameplay feature, but also a gorgeous implementation of the spirit of "Journey to the West". The music and voice acting are top notch. The soundtrack is epic and meditative at the same time, perfectly complementing the atmosphere. Every word and sound seems to be woven into the fabric of an ancient epic. This is a game that you don't just play through — you live it. It evokes delight, awe, and sincere gratitude for the fact that such projects exist. Game Science created not just an action game — they created a cultural bridge between the West and the East, between myth and game. Rating: 10 out of 10. A legend in every pixel.

The game has many flaws but overall it's a solid product. Especially story and lore are delivered with great effort and I'm now interested in Chinese mythology thanks to that. - The initial few hours (after the very cool intro) are a frustrating experience. There is an "optional" troll boss that sucks the fun and patience out of you right from the start when you're not invested in the game yet, which is IMO a big mistake. Shortly thereafter you face one of the hardest bosses in the game (relative to your skill and character level at that time) which is also very frustrating. I quit the game once right then and only came back months later to finish my playthrough. - The game rewards exploration, but there are invisible walls EVERYWHERE, so you constantly run against them, which is annoying. - Character progression is very lackluster. There are many points in the skill tree that don't change much and don't feel exciting. I stayed in one stance for the whole game (besides some testing out) and also kept the very first spirit I got for most of my playthrough, although you get dozens of them. - The game is way too long, so I suggest taking a longer break after a while or you'll probably burn out. Despite all of that the game is still fun and you can tell that the devs wanted to make something good.

?? Black Myth: Wukong – A Dark Mythic Journey Reimagined | Gamer Review ?? As a gamer who’s deeply into immersive storytelling, punishing yet rewarding combat, and rich lore, Black Myth: Wukong took my expectations and shattered them—in the best way possible. This isn't just another soulslike clone or action RPG. This is a myth brought to life with brutal elegance, wrapped in the magic of Chinese folklore, and delivered with the visual flair of a next-gen masterpiece. ?? Combat: Fluid, Brutal, and Deeply Satisfying Right off the bat, the combat in Black Myth: Wukong feels weighty and precise. Every strike counts. It’s not about button-mashing—it’s about rhythm, patience, and strategy. The developers clearly drew inspiration from the Soulsborne genre, but Wukong adds its own unique flair through shape-shifting abilities and mystical staff techniques. You can literally transform mid-combat—into a giant insect, a flame-wielding beast, or even mist to dodge attacks. It’s not just flashy; it’s functional and deeply tied into the game’s lore. Boss battles are a true test of skill and timing, often demanding multiple retries, but never feeling unfair. That “just one more try” feeling is constant, and when you finally land that perfect dodge or combo—pure dopamine. ?? Protagonist: The Monkey King Reborn You play as the Destined One—an interpretation of Sun Wukong, the legendary Monkey King from Journey to the West. But this isn’t a cheeky, light-hearted take. This is a darker, more mysterious Wukong, filled with inner conflict and bound by destiny. The character design, movement, and even voice acting (especially in Mandarin) carry a mythic weight. He’s agile, powerful, and unpredictable—just like the legends. ?? World & Graphics: Unreal Engine 5 Brilliance Visually, Black Myth: Wukong is nothing short of breathtaking. Built on Unreal Engine 5, it delivers insane fidelity—textures, lighting, particle effects, weather systems. It feels like every single frame is art. From haunted temples to bamboo forests filled with spirits, to crumbling mountains haunted by grotesque demons—this game lives and breathes its world. There’s a sense of isolation and awe as you walk through desolate battlefields or encounter godlike enemies hiding in shadows. Exploration rewards curiosity, and there’s always some haunting detail tucked away in a corner. ?? Storytelling: Mythology Meets Mystery The storytelling is cryptic, much like Dark Souls, but heavily steeped in Chinese mythology. If you’re familiar with Journey to the West, you’ll catch a lot of references. But even if you’re not, the game does a great job of making you feel the weight of ancient legends and forgotten curses. Cutscenes are cinematic, voice acting is powerful, and the narrative tone is mature, poetic, and melancholic. ?? Sound & Music: Ethereal & Eerie The soundtrack feels like a forgotten hymn—filled with traditional Chinese instruments, ambient tension, and bursts of adrenaline when fights begin. The sound design builds an immersive layer over the visuals. You feel the wind in the bamboo, the clash of staff on steel, the snarl of corrupted beasts. ?? Verdict: A Must-Play for Soulslike & Mythology Lovers Black Myth: Wukong is more than just a game—it’s an experience. It blends fast-paced action, rich cultural lore, stunning visuals, and challenging gameplay into something that feels fresh yet familiar. It demands patience, skill, and curiosity—and in return, it rewards you with an unforgettable journey. If you love games like Sekiro, Dark Souls, or Nioh, and you’re curious about Eastern mythology, this one should be at the top of your list. ? Rating: 9.5/10 A mythical masterpiece in the making.

Black Myth: Wukong es el viaje mitológico que se siente como un videojuego de leyenda. No es solo un soulslike visualmente impresionante; es una carta de amor al mito más icónico de la literatura china: El Rey Mono, protagonista de Viaje al Oeste. Esta obra, fundamental para la cultura asiática, sirve como columna vertebral narrativa del juego, y Game Science ha sabido transformarla en una experiencia interactiva que mezcla acción, asombro y profundidad mitológica. Encarnar al Rey Mono no es solo ponerse en la piel de un guerrero hábil: es ser un ser entre mundos, un personaje cargado de simbolismo. El báculo mágico (Ruyi Jingu Bang), sus transformaciones animales, su astucia e irreverencia… cada uno de estos elementos ha sido cuidadosamente traducido al lenguaje jugable. Controlar a Wukong se siente ágil, poderoso y, sobre todo, divertido. No hay sensación más gratificante que encadenar ataques con su bastón icónico o convertirse en una criatura mítica para cambiar el ritmo del combate. Cada transformación es tanto una mecánica como un homenaje a su leyenda, lo que refuerza el vínculo entre el mito y la jugabilidad. Aunque el juego comparte ADN con títulos como Sekiro o Lies of P, Black Myth destaca por su identidad propia. Los enemigos, jefes y escenarios están inspirados en demonios, dioses y espíritus de la mitología china, y enfrentarse a ellos no solo es un reto mecánico, sino también una inmersión en un imaginario profundo y distinto. Cada combate tiene un peso simbólico; muchas veces estás enfrentando no solo a una criatura, sino a una idea, a una ense?anza oculta entre líneas mitológicas. El ritmo del juego es sólido: ni demasiado castigador ni indulgente. Aprender los patrones de los enemigos, buscar el momento perfecto para esquivar o contraatacar, y experimentar con las habilidades de Wukong ofrece una curva de aprendizaje adictiva. A eso se suma una dirección artística hipnótica, con paisajes oníricos que parecen sacados de un pergamino antiguo. Conclusión Black Myth: Wukong logra algo extraordinario: hace que jugar sea tan fascinante como el mito que lo inspira. No es solo un gran soulslike; es una reinvención interactiva de uno de los personajes más queridos y complejos de la literatura china. Si te gustan los desafíos con alma, las leyendas antiguas y los juegos que se sienten diferentes, este título no solo es recomendable: es imprescindible.

补条评论 这游戏我其实是预购的，刚解锁的时候兴致勃勃，但缺乏动作游戏的经验，被灵虚子杀了十多次（应该没几个人被灵虚子杀那么多次的吧？），然后在一次一次的努力之下，通了第一章。本是打算一鼓作气通关的，但后来因为有其他事情一天没打开，两天就没打开，然后就半年过去了，过年期间才捡起来继续打。 因为过去了那么久，其实已经从各种渠道了解到了游戏内容，对我来说其实已经没有了太多新鲜感，但自己操控角色实际走在后续的黄风岭、小雷音寺、火焰山之上，还是被美术深深的震撼。 个人最喜欢的是第三章，地图设计和怪物设计都很对我胃口，被冰封的尸体举起手一同指向BOSS的方向、似神似佛似魔的BOSS设计，以及最后提刀杀穿黄眉的那些弟子，真的疯狂到不行！ 黑神话最喜欢的角色是第三章登场的猪八戒，和以前所认识的那些胖猪形象不同，本作的猪八戒是一只矮小的话痨小野猪。主角是那种哑巴角色，从头到尾不会说话，猪八戒的加入让人不再无聊，他一直在那叭叭叭的我觉得还蛮有趣的，他还不止话痨，还挺能打，战斗的时候我经常站在一边看着他那个小矮子抡起钉耙厮杀，还会骂我还不去帮忙真的笑死。 第四章他的主场，跟他打的那两场莫名有种悲壮感，特别是最后的过场动画，更是让我鼻子一酸，原来还能这么写啊。 我不擅长动作游戏，这游戏也没有难度选项，所以我打的还是蛮吃力的，最后使用了一点点的风灵月影力量才通关的（诶嘿） 前面有多喜欢，最终章就有多失望，当我来到花果山，兴致勃勃的踏上筋斗云想着去游览这美丽的世界时，被眼前一览无余的场景惊愕到，第六章的地图设计很难让我想象的出这竟然是和前五章是一个游戏里面的，太潦草了！！就一个大草林！我简直不敢相信！不知道是时间问题，还是什么大人之间的问题，花果山的地图给人的落差感实在太大，无法挽回那种。 打完大圣残躯，开始出现字幕时，我才发现我通关了，我一愣，我还没打二郎神啊！查了一下发现需要做一些前置任务去解锁，但我打游戏的习惯是不会去各异收集和做支线的，所以只打出了戴上金箍的结局 满分10分个人给9分，总的来说，还是非常棒的游戏，扣的那一分是第六章的地图设计，但其他地方的表现真的令人无可挑剔，推荐所有不讨厌动作的人游玩

[h1]齐天大帝，斗战……胜佛！[/h1] 风中的云彩，它向我走来。 远处那个人，还在等待， 熟悉的声音，已不在。 悟空低头嘶吼，来自面前大佛的压力却越来越重，如千座，万座须弥山，往日依仗的高强本领，这一刻竟然如同不存在一般，如钢筋铁骨的不坏之躯，却只如纸糊，笔直的孤拐一点一点弯曲，挺直的脊梁发出不负重堪的声音。 悟空龇牙嘶吼，声音却已经嘶哑。 对面的如来佛祖叹息一声：“痴儿！” 他右掌虚举，朝着悟空缓缓压下，轰的一声，悟空的脚下灵山崩碎，他的双腿扎如石中，微微颤抖，它的臂膀也不再稳如泰山，而是同样随着双腿颤抖着，巨大如倾天之力的压力，让悟空双目迸裂，一行血泪沿着眼角流下。 滴落在地上。 清尘老道士张开口，不知该如何形容眼前的这一幕。 “你说你要离开，明天还会回来？曾经忘不掉的，如今你是否还记得来。转身不算告别，分离却分不开……” 灵山上，仙佛一片沉默之中，在悟空不甘的嘶吼中，似乎有一个声音在唱道。 这时候，它的腰已经被压成了一张紧绷的弓状，脊椎仿佛随时会崩断的样子，那漫天仙佛都提起心来，担心它什么时候，会筋骨折断，压垮在地。 悟空却一寸一寸的迎着如来一掌的压力，直起身来！ 他双目赤红，几乎喷薄出血雾，一字一句的嘶吼道：”打破顽石……不悟空！俺…不…悟！” 如果你是ps5的话，可以说没有对比没有伤害??，ps5画面会比高配pc糊那么一点，而且有些地方明显有卡顿，仅仅是在第一回黑风山游玩的时候肉眼还是能感觉到卡顿，在三种模式中建议还是选择性能模式以尽量稳定在60帧 人眼是自适应的，玩久了其实到还好，毕竟黑神话的画面美术??和细节本身就很高，强大的美术水平弥补了分辨率不足的视觉缺陷 [h2]虚幻5和光追[/h2] 得益于大家期待的虚幻5加持，游戏的模型细节得以最大程度保留，而且咱黑神话可谓万千宠爱于一身，英伟达显卡对它的支持也非常不错，如果你有40系显卡，那开启光追和帧生成就能够获得极佳的画面氛围 对于我个人而言还是光追调低一点好，因为光追带来的阴影和光照对比非常大，很多情况一边超亮一边超黑，很容易引起生理不适。再加上黑神话的美术设计本身就非常之高，除了实地扫描的建模外，诸如土地庙的石版画、敌人boss的形象设计、打斗动画的豪华特效盛宴，这些绝对是业界第一梯队，所以你要问游戏的画面怎样——绝对值得你去欣赏！ [h2]上手门槛[/h2] 你要说咱天命人上手的门槛如何，我得说上手倒是简单，即使是动作游戏新手也能快速适应，但是想玩好真的非常非常难，很多动作游戏都没有棍子武器的主角，所以第一次接触会挥棒子的猴哥这在很长一段时间里都会不适应，像是把握不好距离等等问题，再加上诸如“识破”这种类似弹反的操作极难掌握，玩家的体验就处在低不低高不高的尴尬情况，好在还有很多技能可以使用，像是变身、定身术、分身这些能力，既好用而且种类还多 战斗的教学开场CG还是非常巧妙的，第一是展示了精彩的动作戏，第二呢也能帮助玩家迅速熟悉操作，这第三还交代了大圣“最后的故事”，随着游戏的深入，玩家将逐渐掌握闪避和完美闪避等高级技巧，从而在面对BOSS战时更加从容。但我觉得教程是有问题的 ??第一，没有告诉我什么是棍势，我也是看了很多直播和讲解之后才明白UI右下角的两个豆原来是棍势！ ??第二，“识破”太难用，在刚解锁的那一会我还以为如获至宝，直到我死了一遍又一遍之后开始自我怀疑：这玩意到底咋用？？我也是看了别人讲解之后才搞懂了：“轻击结束再重击再被受击那一瞬间操作才管用” [h2]地图设计和boss战斗[/h2] 这个真的是“一坨屎”了，当然并不能一概否定整体的场景设计，很多道路分支藏着很多有趣事件，而且建模和设计也相当不错。但是之前没有小地图加上大片的空气墙让探索过程十分受罪??！这可能会给部分玩家带来探索上的不便，但同时也增加了探索的乐趣和对环境的沉浸感。此外，游戏的文化内涵和剧情呈现，虽然在某些地方略显生硬，但整体上仍然能够让玩家感受到《西游记》的经典魅力，所以还不赖~ 这是一个bossrush游戏吗？是，但不全是。除了主线还有支线，妖王加头目总共有81位，是不是代表81难呢？这就没有答案了！BOSS战的设计非常具有挑战性，新手村的大头幽魂，第二回拿猴头下酒的虎先锋，难倒了多少玩家！！但游戏也为不同水平的玩家提供了成长的空间。对于新手玩家而言，通过击败小怪来提升等级和购买装备是一个不错的选择。虽然存在一些瑕疵，但瑕不掩瑜

First, to get it out of the way, this game is great. I love it. It's a lot of fun, the story is engaging and memorable, it is *mostly* very polished. I've played through completely several times, and got 100% of the achievements. That being said, the FLAWS in the game are very irritating a best, and stroke-risk levels of infuriating at worst. Starting with minor gripes and "feedback". Most of the crafting materials are able to be purchased after a certain point. There are a couple of materials, however, that MUST be farmed, at least one of which has a terrible drop rate and amount, only drop from ONE enemy type, and those enemies are not only very few, but they aren't really set up along a "farming route". I'm talking about the withered silk-worm. Luckily, you only need it for two medicines, and they aren't super important, but it IS irritating. You only get them from these annoying stone worm things that basically knock you off of your feet, and take a few hits to kill, even with top tier, end game gear. Either making the enemies drop more of the item, make them drop from more enemies, arrange the enemies along a route that is efficient, or MAKE ALL CRAFTING ITEMS PURCHASABLE ONCE YOU BEAT THE GAME AND CONTINUE BEFORE BEGINNING A NEW CYCLE. Respect the player's time, please. Doing things like this may pad out "play time" in some way, but these are the types of things that irk me and a lot of other players. In the same vein, end game crafting materials should be abundant by the end of the second or third play through. I shouldn't have to play through the game 5 times to fully upgrade all of my weapons and armor because one or two crafting materials are only available in specific, limited amounts per play-through. During the first run, that makes sense, but by the end of the second or third, it's ridiculous. This is highlighted by the fact that beyond a certain point, there's nothing you can really do with the excess of "will" (the in-game currency) that you do NOT drop upon death (like in souls games) and have hundreds of thousands of in the end. And while we're at it, it's really dumb that you can't sell UNNEEDED crafting materials that don't "convert to will" on additional play-throughs (which only seems to happen with key items). My inventory is cluttered with BS I can't do anything except watch the stack number raise. Another minor gripe is the fact that there are unskippable cut scenes, either fully rendered or scripted "in-engine" scenes, even in NG+ and beyond. I understand making certain things unskippable during NG, because you want the story to be experienced, but I should have the option to skip ALL cut-scenes from NG+ and beyond. Again, PLEASE RESPECT THE PLAYER'S TIME. I am an adult. I love playing video games. I only have so much time to play them though, and having to sit through repeated, unchanged iterations of the same scenes over again takes away from my enjoyment. The last *minor* gripe is that for some reason, probably the fault of the localization process (maybe?), certain mechanics are poorly explained and unclear. I shouldn't have to google what "seeing through and enemy" means in practice when it's a fairly core mechanic of the game. Or what exactly "might" and "qi" are while playing. And that's aside from the fact that there's no direct way to aquire them, even being impossible without certain items in your build. More aggravating gripes: While the game plays well most of the time, and this may be more of an engine problem, but the game seems to suffer from the EXTREMELY common trend of being under-optimized and assuming that anyone playing the game will have a machine new/powerful enough to compensate for heaving processing. While I NOW have good machines, I didn't always, so I can readily put myself in the shoes of someone with an older PC that wants to enjoy this game, but has to suffer through sudden frame rate drops. While I mostly play games on my desktop PC, I have been traveling with my laptop and playing on it. With a great processor and a 2070 super, I have to use throttlestop and MSI afterburner to overclock things enough to get the game to play decently, using TPFancontrol to lock fan speeds at max in order to keep things cool enough to not thermal throttle. And even then, for some reason, the dialed back settings seem to be overridden in the pause menu, dropping the frame rate from 60 to 8 and often crashing the game, if not my driver. I know most people aren't going to OC their machine, but hasn't been a problem with other games like Lies of P, Elden Ring, RE Village, etc. Next, I don't know about anyone else, but I HATE runbacks to bosses in general. This game mostly doesn't have them, but the few that do exist are OBNOXIOUS. The battle with Giant Shigandang is a good example of this. And speaking of Giant Shigandang... The auto-target system NEEDS WORK. Really, the camera placement needs work. When fighting this GIANT boss, you really need to stay in one area to avoid one-shot kill attacks, while also being close enough to run in and attack when you have the opportunity. For whatever reason, even with auto-target and all associated settings turned off, in that specific area, as the boss moves around, auto-target STILL automatically kicks in but switching, losing, and targeting different parts of the boss, whipping the camera around and often away from where you need to be looking. That also brings up how often the entire screen gets obstructed by the enemy you're fighting, often resulting in taking an outsized amount of damage. This wouldn't be a HUGE problem, except.... If you're going to have a game that is based around dodging with no blocking or parrying mechanic outside of optional skills, you'd better make the timing on those skills AND dodging VERY CONSISTENT. It simply isn't here. The "seeing through" mechanic, for example, requires timing based on where THE ANIMATION is in the middle of a combo, relative to the enemy's attack animation, which is also affected by frame drops. A delayed parry can be fine, like the special parry skill with the sword in Lies of P, but it is consistent and there is an alternative parry/block with that weapon. The timing here is worse than the parry mechanic in Code Vein, which was so bad I just never tried to parry since the parry was delayed, varied in its effective window, and just sucked. However, the other two games had practice dummies, with Lies of P even having one that attacked with consistent timing so you could practice parrying and get used to the timing without needing to go through loading screens to respawn enemies for practice. Now for the MAJOR gripes: This goes for MANY games, most of which I love, even though I hate these things: INPUT READING, ROLL CATCHING, AND UNBLOCKABLE/UNDODGEABLE ANIMATION TRIGGERING ATTACKS ARE NOT A GOOD WAY OF INCREASING DIFFICULTY FOR BOSSES! IT IS JUST LAZY AND INFURIATING. Make the boss faster, more responsive and punishing for button mashing or mistimed healing or dodges, but input reading especially is just infuriating. With the loong dragon in the webbed hollow, you can have the boss entirely stunlocked by your gang of monkey doubles while you charge your heavy attack, and the boss will block your attack every time. This is clear input reading. And don't get me started with the first "final boss" monkey in his final stage. I can be in cloud step, yet get parried EVERY SINGLE TIME if I use a heavy attack. INPUT READING IS LAZY. As for roll catching, the Yin Tiger fight is the worst about this that I can' think of right now. He also pulls the unavoidable, animation triggering brutal attack, but not as bad as Non-Able. All of those things suck, and feel unfair during the fight, like they're just cheating. All of these "difficulty measures" do. In general, the game is great, but it's not perfect, and all of these things make the balance feel off and could be improved upon.

Black Myth: Wukong no es solo un videojuego: es una carta de amor a la leyenda del Rey Mono y una verdadera revolución visual en los títulos de acción RPG. Desde el primer momento, impresiona con su apartado gráfico, tan cinematográfico que cada escenario parece sacado de una pintura china en movimiento. Los detalles en la vegetación, la iluminación dinámica y las animaciones fluidas sumergen al jugador en un mundo tan hermoso como peligroso. El sistema de combate es desafiante y satisfactorio, en la línea de los “soulslike”, pero con su propio giro inspirado en la agilidad y astucia del mítico Sun Wukong. Cada encuentro requiere estrategia, reflejos y aprendizaje constante, lo que convierte a cada victoria en una auténtica recompensa. Además, las transformaciones del protagonista y su abanico de poderes mitológicos aportan una variedad refrescante al gameplay. La narrativa, basada en Viaje al Oeste, equilibra lo épico con lo introspectivo, y logra que conectemos con los dilemas y la evolución del protagonista. El dise?o de enemigos y jefes, muchos extraídos del folklore chino, enriquece aún más esta experiencia culturalmente inmersiva. En resumen, Black Myth: Wukong es una fusión impresionante de arte, jugabilidad exigente y profundidad narrativa. Un título que no solo entretiene, sino que deja huella.

这是我工作几年后唯一通关的游戏。 装了些MOD——切手技优化、100%掉宝率。像给老花眼配了副眼镜，只为看清年少时错过的风景。 游戏很好。金箍棒劈开黄风岭的沙暴时，我听见了自己二十岁的心跳。可越往后走，脚步越沉。筋斗云那关，空荡荡的云雾里只剩赶路的疲惫。最终停在二郎神殿前，手柄搁在积灰的显示器旁，再没拿起来。 为何不打二周目呢。我盯着库里的《黑神话》，突然想起去年整理旧物，在老婆大学相册里看到空白页。她轻描淡写：“那时候总觉得以后有的是时间拍照。” 原以为男人的遗憾是显卡跑不动新游戏，现在才懂，是4090的光追照不进三十岁的黄昏。少年时翻墙逃课打通《仙剑》的精力，早被地铁通勤碾成粉末；曾经为隐藏BOSS反复练习的耐心，如今在短视频十五秒切换里消磨殆尽。 没打完的二郎神，像极了老婆衣柜里没拆封的旗袍。我们都在最好的年纪，误以为青春是取之不尽的点数。 ——致所有还能为游戏熬夜的年轻人： 趁教室后窗的阳光还没移走， 趁BOSS战的配乐仍在血液里燃烧。 去通关，去拍照，去失败一百次。 有些战斗，错过就是永远； 有些美丽，过期不作保存。

## 破妄求真：《黑神话：悟空》—— 一场颠覆西游的暗黑朝圣之旅 当金箍棒撕裂云层，砸向的不只是妖魔鬼怪，更是我们对《西游记》四百年的集体想象。游戏科学工作室以孤注一掷的勇气，用《黑神话：悟空》这部现象级作品，完成了国产3A游戏零的突破——它不只是技术奇观的展示，更是一场对东方神话的解构与重构，在暗黑史诗的肌理中叩问信仰与存在的本质。 **颠覆重构：神佛崩塌的暗黑宇宙** 游戏彻底颠覆了取经神话的明媚外衣。昔日慈悲的漫天诸佛化为冰冷机械的“金身”，灵山雷音寺沦为布满锈迹与管道的异化空间。主角“天命人”所见的西游真相，是神佛秩序崩塌后的荒诞图景：黄眉老祖假扮如来布道，口中念诵着“既见未来，为何不拜”的扭曲箴言；盘丝洞的百目魔君褪去妖怪皮囊，化身华丽而腐朽的古典舞者。这些设计并非为暗黑而暗黑，而是以视觉冲击力解构权力话语——当神圣沦为虚妄，信仰本身便成为最锋利的枷锁。 **战斗诗篇：棍影中的东方暴力美学** 作为动作游戏的核心，《黑神话》将中国武术美学发挥到极致。金箍棒不再是万能神器，而是需要精确操控的重量级武器。轻重击组合衍生出劈、捅、扫、挑等真实棍术，配合七十二变系统（铜头铁臂、聚形散气等），在电光石火间编织出充满策略性的战斗芭蕾。尤其令人震撼的是Boss战设计：雪地中与赤尻马猴的生死对决，棍棒交击震落松枝积雪；盘丝洞内百目魔君千手齐发的压迫感，让每一次闪避都如刀尖起舞。这些战斗不仅是技巧的考验，更是对东方志怪美学的动态诠释。 **视听炼狱：地狱级的神话场景复现** 游戏凭借虚幻引擎5技术，打造了一座移动的东方奇幻博物馆。山西晋城玉皇庙二十八宿彩塑在游戏中化作狰狞Boss，重庆大足石刻的千手观音被解构成机械佛国，雪幕中的小西天古建群在月光下泛着幽蓝寒光。更令人拍案的是音乐设计：第二章黄风岭战役中，当黄风怪现出本相，高亢悲凉的秦腔《杀伐》骤然炸响，古老唱腔与现代电音碰撞出直击灵魂的史诗感。这些元素共同构建了一个既熟悉又陌生的神话炼狱。 **文化自觉：一场孤勇者的豪赌** 在手游当道的市场环境下，游戏科学抵押房产开发主机游戏的孤注一掷，本身就暗合了悟空反抗天庭的悲壮内核。团队对传统文化的考据堪称苛刻——从古建斗拱比例到敦煌壁画色彩，从山西铙钹戏到广西傩舞面具，每一帧都流淌着文化自觉的血液。当玩家在结尾字幕看到“山西古建筑保护研究所”等机构名单时，方能理解这不仅是游戏，更是一场用数字技术抢救文化遗产的壮举。 《黑神话：悟空》的终极叩问恰如游戏中反复出现的台词：“敢问路在何方？”它用暗黑叙事撕开神话的糖衣，在神性废墟之上重建属于凡人的英雄之路——那条路不在灵山雷音寺的虚妄金顶，而在每个挥棍破除心魔的瞬间。当最后一棒砸向虚伪的“未来佛”，我们终于懂得：真正的西游真经，从来不是赐予的经文，而是用金箍棒在荆棘中劈出的、那条名为“不信天命”的血路。

《黑神话：悟空》作为国产首部3A级动作游戏，以**顶级美术表现与战斗设计**惊艳登场：基于虚幻5引擎打造的东方奇幻世界，场景细节与粒子特效（如云层、火焰）堪称视觉盛宴，搭配沉浸式配乐，完美还原《西游记》的暗黑美学。战斗系统以**“棍势”资源管理为核心**，融合劈、立、戳三种棍法派生与变身、仙术等机制，操作深度与博弈感兼具，但输入延迟及锁定视角问题影响流畅性。**高难度Boss战设计亮眼**，如赤尻马猴、晦月魔君等兼具演出张力与策略性，但小怪分布失衡与“粪怪”设定（如毒蛇群）破坏节奏。技术层面争议显著：**优化问题突出**，PS5火焰/冰雪场景掉帧频繁，PC低配闪退频发（RTX20系以下需降画质），且空气墙、地图引导缺失导致探索体验割裂。叙事采用碎片化手法，剧情动机薄弱引发两极评价，但结局情感冲击力强。总体而言，作为游戏科学处女作，其以**文化厚度与工业水准树立国产标杆**，虽有关卡设计青涩、优化瑕疵等短板，仍以82分MC均分印证国际竞争力。

This game is... something. I have no clue about "Journey to the west", so the story told in the game can be much different for people that actually know it. I will only comment on the gameplay of this game and it's a huge mess. The exploration part of the game is terrible, either areas are big and empty or small and packed, failing to reach a good balance between both extremes. Some parts of areas seem explorable, but aren't, creating the illusion of adventure but in reality you just walk on a big linear path with some branches that might end up on the same path again. In the end you will spend hours with walking on these paths so you don't miss anything. The world is huge, you are small, so walking feels incredibly slow, even when sprinting. The fights are decent and fun... kind of. You can use light attacks & heavy attacks. There are 3 fighting styles, where the light attacks stay the same and the heavy attack changes: you either jump & strike, stand on your staff (giving you damage reduction and protection from attacks on the ground, but hits on the staff reduce your stamina) or make a step and stab the enemy with your staff. Unfortunately, most fights are already over before they start, because channeling your heavy attack before engaging an enemy will result in a oneshot or a very short fight. This is even worse if you take your spells into account. You can turn into stone, reflecting an attack from the enemy, paralyse them for a few seconds, disable your spells to gain more stats, summon clones of yourself or transform into certain enemies (and more). So basicially every non-bossfight is over after Charged Heavy attack+paralyse+attacks. But that's not everything, certain enemies can drop their "souls", allowing you to use them with QI so you transform into them and make a single attack. They can be very bad, good or sometimes even OP & can be upgraded. So you have a ton of tools to use, create your own build and have a fun time... not. The tools are blessing and curse at the same time, because if YOU can use all these tools, how can bosses have a chance? Well, they don't, most of the time, many bosses are just forgettable and not noteworthy, sometimes you can even fight multiple bosses in a row without any issues. Sometimes you even fight 4 Bosses in 5 minutes. This is the huge majority of the bosses. But other bosses, most of the story bosses, are just painfully cheap and unfun. Don't get me wrong, the game is neither easy nor hard, the difficulty is decently set, even most of the "cheap and unfun" bosses are beatable in around 5 tries even without changing your equipment or build. But standing still for a minute, watching the enemy do his attacks, getting attacked, teleporting behind you, chaining them into attacks, sucht that even the focused cam can't keep up properly with the boss, big explosions left and right , burning areas on the ground, small enemies jumping on you, flying into the air throwing lighting strikes on you or whatever the boss wants to do, gaining invincibility mid fight for a few seconds so your big attack doesn't deal any damage, almost undodgeable mid fight cutscenes that cost you 50% of your hp, is one of the most frustrating things I have ever witnessed in any game. And even if you beat every boss in this game: There is no satisfaction. You haven't beaten a boss against all odds, you beat a nuiscance in your way that's getting on your nerves. You will end up looking for cheese windows: Maybe you can burst the enemy before starting his 2nd phase, maybe you can stagger him out of some attack, maybe if you use your clones you can deal enough damage, it's just the way this game makes you think. And unfortunately: This is the biggest downside of this game. It would be MUCH better if it was just an Action RPG. Because this game isn't a soulslike. it's an action RPG that wants to be a soulslike so badly without going the whole mile. Personally, the cinematic boss fights don't match well with the soulslike structure of the game, even though you don't lose anything when you die. If I play an Action RPG and die, with huge cinematics mid fight, multiple phases then I want to go back into the fight IMMEDIATELY. I don't want to walk 2 minutes, I don't want to clear enemies on the way, I don't want to redo the first phase of the boss which - ironically- sometimes this game even does. E.g. the final boss has multiple phases and midway through the fight is a "checkpoint", such that you don't have to do the whole thing at once. It's a weird mix of a "classic" action RPG like a God of War while still trying to appeal to the core soulslike fans and fails imo miserably by achieving neither in a good way. It's not a bad game by any means. But if you go into this game expecting a "soulslike masterpiece" how some people describe it, you will be disappointed, because it can clearly not measure up to other big names in the soulslike category because the game is far from any soulslike experience out there. Sometimes the expectations you bring into a game can severly influence the way how you experience the game, for me it worsened it. The game is well made, you have many different enemies, the art looks pretty good, every chapter is finished with a nice animation that looks REALLY good. But I couldn't enjoy it. I played through it because I wanted to understand why so many people loved this game so much, but even after finishing it, I just can't understand it. Maybe it's my expectation, maybe the gameplay and style of the game are just not my cup of tea, maybe knowing journey to the west might improve this game for me. In the end, it doesn't matter. I'm glad it's finally over, Chapter 3 is just a big pile of **** and should be removed, chapter 6 for the most part was a mistake, strike style & the first QI skill you get is the best, why even bother using anything else. "not recommending" this game would be unfair, because it still is a decent game with (for me) huge flaws that impact the experience very much. So I recommend it, but people should know what to expect when buying this game, especially with a more negative impression like mine.

《黑神话：悟空》在画面上的表现堪称惊艳，UE5 引擎的强大性能在游戏中发挥得淋漓尽致。从踏入游戏的那一刻起，玩家便仿佛置身于一个真实的东方神话世界。? 游戏中的场景建模精细入微，每一处细节都处理得恰到好处。黑风山中，树木的纹理清晰可见，仿佛能触摸到岁月留下的痕迹；岩石上的青苔，绿意盎然，为整个场景增添了生机与真实感。而水体效果更是令人拍案叫绝，溪流清澈透亮，潭底的石块和青苔清晰倒映在水中，涟漪的动态效果自然而逼真。当角色踏足水面，水波荡漾，那种身临其境的感觉让人难以忘怀。? 场景的氛围营造也十分出色，充分展现了东方意境。在泛着灰蓝色雾气的山林中，松、柏、竹若隐若现，宛如一幅写意的水墨画。幽静的山坳里，翠绿的水潭宛如一块温润的碧玉，散发着神秘的气息。登上山顶，初升的太阳将山尖染成粉红，那壮丽的景色让人不禁感叹大自然的鬼斧神工。? 战斗演出和动画过场同样精彩绝伦。战斗中的一镜到底设计，让玩家能够全身心地投入到激烈的战斗中，感受战斗的紧张与刺激。而巨型 BOSS 的登场，更是带来了震撼的视觉冲击。建筑、天命人与 BOSS 同屏出现，尽管体积差异巨大，但都保持了极高的建模精度，展现了游戏科学强大的技术实力。? 章节之间的前情提要与后记，采用了多种独特的动画风格，如手绘、木偶戏、吉卜力等，讲述了丰富的故事，配上专属的优质 BGM，为玩家带来了一场视觉与听觉的盛宴。这些间章故事的呈现方式在游戏中独树一帜，艺术成分与叙事信息量之大令人赞叹。

本人目前四十多小时，一周目第五章快打完了。配置是隐星g16，4070，显存8g，全影视级无光追全地图的平均帧率在五十多左右。但开了中等光追就吃不消了，而且此时由于原始帧太低，会出现植被闪烁的情况。下面结合我个人游玩经验简单评价下对这游戏的看法∶ 优点∶画质好，美术好，融合了很多我们中国传统文化的元素在里面，比如说怪物的外形设计，狼妖、蛇精等等。音乐和配音都是顶级的。有些boss战的演出效果也非常棒，比如打黄眉大王的时候，会有天命人在阁楼上变得很小，被黄眉注视着的场景，感觉自己身处戏中十分渺小，命运为他人掌握；再比如黄风大王开二阶段的时候，黄沙漫天，遮云蔽日。游戏中还有一些boss对打的场景，相当于游戏自带的电子斗蛐蛐，比如石先锋和石敢当对打，我们作为天命人可以坐收渔翁之利。法宝系统也很有意思，四个法宝分别针对四个章节的boss起到克制效果，而且和原著也很贴合。 缺点∶这游戏刚发售的时候有很多人说场景辨识度差，容易找不到路，但现在游戏中已经出了地图，结合我目前的游戏体验来看，这个缺点基本上被解决掉了。对于我来说最大的缺点是某些boss的设计实在是糟糕。第一个，大型boss的交互性很差，除去一些人说的飞行boss锁定视角乱飘的缺点，还有就是由于boss体型的增大，往往意味着他们的位移比天命人的位移远的多，这就导致很容易空棍，打起来非常不爽，特别是第四章蜘蛛精那个死老太婆，扭来扭去的，明明看着能砸到的，一打下去又闪开了。第二个，很多人觉得双boss战的设计很好，但我却觉得很差劲，原因是游科强制性的让你不能先打死其中一个boss，而必须要两个boss的血量交替消耗，可能是为了演出效果考虑。据我目前所知，严格来说只有第五章有三对双boss战设计（电子斗蛐蛐不算），后两对都存在我上面说的问题。按照正常的逻辑来说，有两个boss，我们肯定想的是先打死其中一个吧，但游科偏不让你这么做，你打掉第一个boss一定血量后，视角会自动锁定到第二个boss身上，而且会通过某种手段让你无法再打到第一个boss，除非你打掉第二个boss一些血量。比如云里雾雾里云，当你打掉其中一个一部分血后，它就会进入隐身，换第二个上，直到你把第二个打掉一定血。掀烘兴，兴烘掀就更离谱了，当你打掉其中一个boss一定血自动切换锁定后，如果你说我非要犟我非要先打死这一个，那么你有可能会触发打死一个boss后无法对第二个boss造成伤害的bug，而且这个bug到现在也没修复。此外，游戏的第五章存在比较严重的换皮怪现象，有赶工的嫌疑。

因为忙于生活，只能每天下班之后抽出一点时间打打黑猴，好在紧赶慢赶，赶在6.18折扣前打完了一周目，好吧，感觉自己还是大怨种。整个游戏中我最喜欢的章节应该要算第二章节黄风岭，整个荒漠的氛围、灵吉菩萨的说书，刚开始还未褪去的激情，一遍又一遍磨砺自己通过的虎先锋后的成就感，真的没有办法形容。其次就是第五章火焰山了，好评给到萍萍和牛夫人，牛夫人真的太顶了。说实话，打到第四章的时候产生了很强烈的失望感，尤其是买了豪华版，并且得知原本有十二个章节的时候，就经常会有一种感觉——我花了三百多就买了个这？从游戏性上来说，黑猴中规中矩，这稀碎的操作手感，不支持改键、武器建模单一，战斗方式单调，这些都是在游戏过程中能够真切感受到的，但还是断断续续的玩了下来。（当然我懂，菜就多练）黑猴如果只看游戏性游戏内容的话，只能说游科还有很多地方需要打磨，成长的空间也很大。可是后面的内容确实的的确确地震撼到我了，无论是音乐、美术、还是剧本设计都是完美的恰到好处，一场场盛大的演出，让我明白了什么叫做第九艺术。黑猴也许不是一款好的ARPG，但是无愧于第九艺术的美誉。如果你冲着游戏本身来的话，黑猴可能会让你失望。但是如果你抱着一个欣赏艺术看电影的心情，那黑猴里的故事会打动每一个知晓西游记的人。最后与大圣残躯打斗的演出，真的很震撼。无论是如意金箍棒的出现，还是音乐的响起。有那么一瞬间我仿佛回到了那个守着破电视剧的小时候，看着荧光屏幕里，披着披风，手拿金箍棒的盖世英雄似乎重新回到了我的生活。

中式神话与3A游戏的激情碰撞 《黑神话：悟空》自亮相以来，便凭借其独特的东方神话背景与惊艳的实机演示，在全球游戏爱好者的心中种下了一颗期待的种子。如今，这颗种子终于开花结果，游戏正式上线，它是否达到了玩家们的预期？是否能为国产3A游戏开辟出一条崭新的道路？让我们一同深入《黑神话：悟空》的世界，一探究竟。 一、剧情：在传统与创新中重塑西游 游戏巧妙地基于《西游记》进行大胆改编，将玩家带入一个暗黑风格浓郁的西游世界。在这里，你不再是那个神通广大、一路降妖除魔的齐天大圣，而是以“天命人”的视角，重走西行之路，见证神、妖、佛之间复杂的恩怨情仇。剧情以一种非线性叙事的方式展开，主线故事紧凑且充满悬念，支线任务则丰富了游戏世界的细节与深度，让玩家在探索过程中不断发现隐藏在神话背后的真相 。 例如，在某个支线任务中，玩家会遇到一位看似普通的村民，随着对话的深入，却发现他与一段尘封已久的神妖大战有着千丝万缕的联系，这种层层递进的剧情设计，极大地激发了玩家的好奇心与探索欲。不过，剧情在部分情节的衔接上稍显生硬，一些角色的行为动机缺乏足够的铺垫，使得玩家在理解上存在一定的障碍 。 二、画面：虚幻5引擎下的东方美学盛宴 得益于虚幻5引擎的强大性能，《黑神话：悟空》的画面表现堪称一绝。游戏对场景的还原度极高，从雄伟壮丽的花果山，到阴森诡异的地府，再到庄严肃穆的雷音寺，每一处场景都细节满满，仿佛将玩家带入了一个真实的神话世界。运用Nanite虚拟微多边形技术，游戏中建筑、山石等模型的面数达到千万级别，纹理质感细腻逼真，即便是一块普通的石头，也能看到岁月侵蚀的痕迹 。 光照效果更是为画面增色不少，动态光影下，角色与场景的互动更加自然，白天的阳光明媚、夜晚的月光皎洁、战斗时的法术光芒，都营造出了极强的氛围感。比如在一场激烈的战斗中，技能的光影特效与周围环境相互映衬，让玩家身临其境。然而，在一些复杂场景中，游戏会出现轻微的卡顿现象，对玩家的流畅体验造成了一定影响 。 三、玩法：战斗与养成的深度融合 战斗是《黑神话：悟空》的核心玩法，其打击感十足，动作流畅自然。玩家可以使用金箍棒进行多样化的攻击，轻攻击、重攻击、蓄力攻击、连招等组合丰富，配合灵活的闪避、格挡与弹反机制，让战斗节奏紧张刺激。游戏还引入了七十二变的设定，玩家可以化身各种妖怪，获得独特的技能与能力，为战斗增添了更多策略性与趣味性 。 养成系统同样丰富，玩家可以通过完成任务、击败敌人获取经验值升级，提升属性。收集材料打造和强化装备，不同装备有着独特的属性与外观。天赋系统提供了多种加点方向，玩家可以根据自己的战斗风格进行个性化培养。不过，游戏在操作手感上还有一定的优化空间，比如在快速切换技能时，偶尔会出现操作延迟的情况 。 四、角色：经典形象的全新演绎 游戏中的角色设计令人眼前一亮，孙悟空、唐僧、猪八戒、沙僧等经典形象都进行了重新诠释，既保留了原著中的特点，又赋予了他们更加丰富的性格与背景故事。孙悟空不再是那个单纯的叛逆者，他在游戏中经历了迷茫、挣扎与成长，让玩家看到了一个更加立体的齐天大圣 。 而游戏中众多的妖怪形象也极具特色，它们造型各异，每个妖怪都有自己独特的攻击方式与背景设定，比如黄风岭的黄风怪，其攻击招式与风元素紧密结合，战斗时黄沙漫天，给玩家带来了强烈的视觉冲击 。 五、音乐音效：奏响神话世界的天籁之音 音乐音效是《黑神话：悟空》的一大亮点，配乐由知名音乐人打造，融合了中国传统音乐元素与现代音乐风格，为游戏营造出了浓郁的东方氛围。战斗时激昂的旋律，让玩家热血沸腾；探索时悠扬的曲调，又让玩家沉浸于游戏世界的宁静与神秘 。 音效方面，游戏对环境音效、技能音效、角色语音等细节处理得十分到位。金箍棒挥舞时的呼呼风声、技能释放时的轰鸣声、角色的对话声，都让玩家仿佛置身于神话世界之中，增强了游戏的沉浸感 。 《黑神话：悟空》无疑是一款具有里程碑意义的国产游戏，它在剧情、画面、玩法、角色、音乐音效等方面都有着出色的表现，为玩家呈现了一个极具魅力的东方神话世界。尽管存在一些小瑕疵，但它的出现，无疑为国产3A游戏的发展注入了一剂强心针，让我们看到了国产游戏在国际舞台上绽放光芒的潜力 。

Bought this immediately after coming back from a trip to Japan; this game managed to illicit some of the same feelings of awe and spiritual-depth that I experienced touring some of the Buddhist museums and temples. This game is an artistic feast of eastern-mythology inspired landscapes and character designs. Each creature has a well-written eastern inspired parable for the philosophical idea behind the creature and it's human-based features that lead to its awakening, downfall, or both. These deities are not above the follies of mankind, in fact, throughout we see examples of how humanity plants the seeds of its own downfall through cause-and-effect, and navigating through events with less than skillful means. The game-play design philosophy of souls games lend themselves very well to an almost meditative session and this game heightens that with it's use of deep Buddhist themes and landscapes (alongside Taoism, Confucianism, and more general chinese mythology and philosophical schools of thought). It's worth doing a deep dive into some of the character's portrayed and their historical context and relevance, --- Side note, but Buddhism at its core is a philosophy based on self-awareness, critical thought, insight, the cultivation of wisdom, compassion and harmony as a means to transcend the suffering that is a natural part of life. I just find it beautiful and inspiring that throughout history, even as the representations of these ideas such as temples, sculptures, statues and more have been burned to the ground in an attempt to snuff out its light, largely due to futile attempts at nationalism, grabs of power, or other more egoic pursuits, the central ideas behind it burn brighter than ever and continue to adapt and spread its message through great works of art such as this one. The failed attempts to destroy it have only made it rebuild stronger and ring out truer in the face of further evidence of how futile it is to lean into some of mankind's more unskillful psychological traps such as aversion, desire, or ignorance. The truth of our human reality is self-evident. It doesn't need to be told to you, because if you live enough lifetimes, you'll eventually connect the dots and settle into it on your own. --- Rewarding patience, mastery over mind and emotional states of frustration and panic lead to a feeling of inner achievement and contentment. Exploration is fun, and items and experience lend way to a deep character building system centered around staff-combat, which I'm personally a huge fan of. Music and environmental sound are also a highlight and add considerably to the aesthetic. I was not familiar with the original story this is adapted from "Journey to The West" but this has inspired me to buy the collection and start reading it. I think absorbing this material and then returning to this game at a later time will give me an even greater appreciation for the story it's trying to tell. Lastly, I want to give mention to the use of mixed media in the spots in between chapters to reinforce the themes of each section. The artists, musicians, and animators did a beautiful job and I looked forward to seeing each one. Overall one of my favorite souls-like games just from a first play-through, I imagine my appreciate will grow with time to reflect and experience subsequent play-throughs.

救命！家人们谁懂啊！《黑神话：悟空》真的把我爽到飞起！一进游戏我直接惊了，这场景简直像开了时空传送门！古寺的砖瓦缝里都透着历史味儿，风吹树叶沙沙响，阳光从破窗洒进来，连灰尘都看得清清楚楚，我好几次都忍不住停下来截图，这哪是玩游戏，根本就是沉浸式逛古迹！ 剧情也超带感！我本以为就是打打怪闯关，结果越玩越上头！跟着主角一路探险，遇到各种奇奇怪怪的人和事儿，时不时还冒出几句超有韵味的台词，把西游故事玩出了新花样。有些剧情转折真的绝了，我好几次都被震撼到，满脑子都是 “原来还能这样”！ 怪物设计更是绝绝子！一路上遇到的妖怪，每个都长到我审美点上！有阴森诡异的树妖，挥动藤蔓的样子就像八爪鱼疯狂甩触手；还有霸气十足的牛魔王，一出场直接地震，那体型比我高大好几倍，技能放出来整个屏幕都在晃！更绝的是每个妖怪都有自己的故事和背景，我边打边疯狂脑补，感觉自己不是在玩游戏，而是真的在取经路上降妖除魔！ 战斗手感更是没得说，抡棍子的时候 “呼呼” 带风，闪避妖怪攻击的瞬间肾上腺素飙升！三套棍势随便切换，配合各种法术和变身，每次打 Boss 都像在打一场史诗级战役，虽然被虐得死去活来，但打赢的那一刻真的成就感爆棚！真心安利给所有人，这游戏不玩真的血亏！ —————————————————————— Guys, you have no idea how blown away I am by Black Myth: Wukong! Right from the moment I started playing, I was floored—it felt like I’d been teleported into another world! The ancient temples look so incredibly real, with every crack in the bricks oozing history. When the wind rustles the leaves, or sunlight streams through broken windows, you can even see the dust particles floating in the air. I couldn’t help but pause to take screenshots multiple times—it’s less like playing a game and more like exploring ancient ruins in person! The storyline is insanely gripping! I thought it’d just be about slaying monsters and clearing levels, but I got completely hooked. As I followed the protagonist on his adventure, I encountered all sorts of strange characters and events. The dialogue is full of poetic charm, breathing new life into the classic Journey to the West tale. Some plot twists left me speechless, and I kept thinking, “How did they come up with this?!” The monster designs are out of this world! Every single creature I’ve faced is right up my alley. There’s this eerie tree demon whose vines whip around like an octopus going wild, and then there’s the fearsome Bull Demon King—when he shows up, the ground literally shakes! He towers over my character, and his attacks fill the entire screen. What’s even cooler is that each monster has its own backstory. I couldn’t stop imagining all the lore as I fought them—it truly felt like I was on a real pilgrimage to subdue demons! The combat feels amazing too. Swinging the staff makes this satisfying “whoosh” sound, and dodging enemy attacks gets my adrenaline pumping. With three stances to switch between and all those spells and transformations, every boss fight is like an epic showdown. Sure, I got crushed multiple times, but the rush of victory when I finally beat them? Absolutely worth it! I’m telling everyone—you’re seriously missing out if you don’t play this game!

Black Myth: Wukong — красивый удар по нервам.Скажу честно: я очень долго ходил вокруг этой игры. То подумаю: ?ну её, слишком сложная?, то посмотрю трейлер — и снова не могу оторваться. Душа тянулась, а разум твердил: ?Это же Souls-like!? А я к таким играм отношусь с опаской — не то чтобы совсем чужды, но пробовал шедевры Миядзаки и бросал спустя пару часов. Но в какой-то момент всё сошлось. Решился. Начал играть. И — да, местами было тяжело. Где-то по двадцать раз загружался. Иногда бесился. Иногда думал бросить, но потом снова включал. И, чёрт возьми, прошёл. Где-то за сорок часов. Без гордости, но с чувством, что это было настоящее приключение. ?? Визуал: восточная сказка на стероидах. Это одна из самых красивых игр, в которые я играл. И нет, это не просто ?на уровне? — это визуальный праздник. Леса, тропики, пустыни, снежные хребты — всё выглядит как живописные полотна, которые вдруг начали дышать и двигаться. Причём каждая локация не просто разная — она будто из другого мира, со своей атмосферой и душой. На ультра-настройках Black Myth буквально оживает. Листья шелестят, пыль летает, свет играет на поверхности воды. Иногда я просто останавливался, чтобы постоять и посмотреть вдаль. Да, встречал отзывы, что мол, графика не топ — ну, не знаю. У меня — визуальный восторг, на 100%. ?? Сюжет: красиво, непонятно, но чертовски атмосферно. Если говорить откровенно — я не понял сюжета вообще. То есть совсем. Ни хрена. Кто с кем воюет, зачем все эти духи, монахи, божественные обезьяны и демоны — я просто плыл по течению. Катсцены шли — я смотрел. Внимательно. С интересом. Но понимал из этого чуть больше, чем ничего. Иногда казалось, что я случайно включил четвёртый сезон сериала, пропустив три предыдущих. Потом я узнал, что всё это основано на китайском эпосе ?Путешествие на Запад?. Да, классика, да, Великий Мудрец (он же Обезьяна), да, куча отсылок и символизма. Но чтобы это всё прочувствовать — надо, наверное, быть знакомым с оригиналом, а лучше — родиться где-нибудь в Хэнани. Я же, как обычный игрок, в сюжет просто не въехал. Но — и это важно — это не мешало получать удовольствие. Игра как будто говорит тебе: ?Ты не понял? Ну и ладно. Смотри, как красиво!? Так я и делал. Атмосфера — мощная. Это как слушать оперу на незнакомом языке: смысл мимо, но эмоции — в самое сердце. ?? Боевая система: перекаты, стойки, адреналин. Боевка — сильная сторона игры. Сначала — тяжеловато. Потом — затягивает. Ты постоянно учишься. Враги разные, приёмы тоже. Игра не даёт расслабиться. Отдача от ударов могла бы быть сочнее, но зато здесь огромное разнообразие стоек, способностей, сборок. И всё это можно на лету менять, перераспределять, экспериментировать. Я, честно, не лез глубоко. Выбрал стиль, вкачал силу, выносливость, ману, откат способностей — и пошёл. Моя тактика: заморозка → удар → перекат → двойник → невидимость → удар. По кругу. И знаешь, работало. Иногда красиво, иногда — в панике, но почти всегда с кайфом. Особенно когда побеждаешь того, кто минут десять назад тебя размазал как масло по экрану. ???♂? Боссы: от ярости до восторга. Боссов здесь огромное количество. Не просто обязательные — куча скрытых, загадочных, запрятанных черт знает где. Иногда я чувствовал себя не героем, а каким-то археологом. Вертикальный левел-дизайн, потайные тропы, непонятные проходы. Местами — вообще без шансов найти без гайда. Помню, один момент с ?погремушкой? — ну вот как я должен был до этого додуматься? А паучий уровень, я там постоянно терялся и потратил кучу времени искав все секреты. Но всё это окупается. Каждый найденный босс — как отдельная награда. Каждое сражение — как экзамен. Бывает, убиваешь с первой попытки. Бывает — умираешь раз за разом, в приступе отчаяния. Но потом приходит момент… и ты побеждаешь. И вот тут уже не игра выигрывает у тебя — а ты у неё. ?? Особенные моменты: эпик за гранью экрана. Отдельно — про скрытую битву с божествами. Это не просто бой. Это целая сцена. Постановка. Кино. Огромные масштабы, небо, титаны, магия, удар за ударом. Я сидел с открытым ртом. Не потому что сложно — нет, она не самая тяжёлая. А потому что зрелищно, мощно, вдохновляюще. Напомнило лучшие бои из Final Fantasy XVI, но с душой китайского эпоса. ?? Темп, усталость и возвращение. Признаюсь, после второй главы я устал. Игра не только сложная, она ещё и морально нагружает. Нужно быть в ней. И когда ты вылетаешь — тяжело вернуться. Я сделал паузу. Думал, заброшу. Но нет. Вернулся. И проглотил оставшиеся главы с жадностью. Финальные битвы прошёл залпом. И знаешь — это было правильно. Это был мой финальный рывок. Игра меня не подвела. ?? Вывод: неидеально, но не забудется Black Myth: Wukong — это не всем. Тут нет простого сюжета. Тут нет пощады. Тут не будет “на расслабоне”. Но если ты хочешь опыта, хочешь испытания, хочешь красоты и боли в одном флаконе — ты должен попробовать. Да, я не понял, что вообще происходило в этой игре. Но я это прочувствовал. Я злился, восхищался, страдал, побеждал. И это важнее любой сюжетной раскладки. Моя оценка — 7 из 10, но с сердцем, которое шепчет: ?Эй, ты справился. Это было что-то?.

This is a moment in which I wish Steam offered a neutral review. I know at this point it's been said to the point of mantra on these Steam pages, but this is a game that deserves a 'it's alright'. Center stage for the game is presentation. It's definitely one of the best looking games released in recent memory, blending a stylized look with elements of reality for a very interesting mix. The opening of the game made my jaw drop in its scale and bombastic energy, something which peppers each step of the way in Black Myth: Wukong. Animations are fluid and full of character. All of the designs from the environments to the NPCs are hand crafted with a specificity denoting a clear sense of art direction that comes together in a cohesive manner rarely seen in Black Myth's contemporaries. Less interesting is combat, which does offer a lot of versatility in its systems. There's depth here to make a lot of different kinds of builds, some of them wildly absurd. One of the primary issues with combat is that it's imprecise. Dodging can be spammed on most occasions, even during some of the most difficult battles, and boss 'tells' start to become unclear underneath a lot of particle spectacle. On top of that, there's a lack of consistency about what constitutes your magic moves actually working or not. This issue is buried in the design DNA of the game play, with a portion of the game not allowing you to fall off cliffs, and then suddenly you can fall off cliffs in a different location. Rules change mid battle with vague indicators of why or how a mechanic has changed. It shares a lot in common with Dark Souls 2 in this regard, which I'm sure has been echoed elsewhere, but I feel it needs to be said again. Controls are a mixed bag. Lack of input on health gourds with them sometimes working and sometimes not, leading to a few deaths that feel cheap. Combos are responsive, and the layout of everything is good. Often times mid boss battle you're sucked into an attack you can't do anything about, and you still take damage for it. I'm not sure exactly what the controller issue/user issue is, but there should be a way to get out of everything. Maybe I didn't understand something correctly, but the game didn't explain it very well either. The story is not compelling. Don't get me wrong, not many of us are showing up to this game for the story, but it needed to be said that there's little here that makes sense if you don't know Journey to the West. Game Science gives you a lot of material to read and put it together if you want, so it is Souls-like in that regard, but nothing exactly hopped out to me personally. There wasn't a sense of mystery like a puzzle I felt compelled to put together, it just felt like I was missing a lot of context that I had no interest in following through on. Others will obviously feel different about the story, but it just wasn't for me. All in all, Black Myth: Wukong is a game I do actually enjoy, but it's got a lot of issues that bring the experience down to what constitutes a mediocre action game with an above average presentation. It's a great introductory game to people that are wanting to get more into Souls-like games, as its much more forgiving than a lot of the others. There just isn't anything here other than the presentation that I haven't seen done better elsewhere. It's alright, but it leaves a lot to be desired.

The opening scene of this game is unbelievable...SO good it hooked me. Then there are the skills that seem to apply on the basis of a RNG so you don't really know if the skill is going to apply. Just look at the application of Resolute Stance. Then there are things like Immobiliation...sometimes it just does not apply...or it applies for a random amount of time. Then there is the timing issue with dodges. Again, sometimes the timing works...sometimes it does not...again it feels like there is a RNG behind this mechanic. If I just wanted a RNG activity i would sit in front of a slot machine. This game had potential, but the designers spent too much time on crafting long winded descriptions of each mob you encounter (along with poems) than they did on making the mechanics work. I would pass on this title.

Хэй-хэй, смертные! Это ваш Великий Мудрец, Равный Небу, Разгоняющий Тучи… ну, в общем, та самая Обезьяна, которая прошла эту игру. И знаете что? Мне не понравилось. Ну, ладно, чуть-чуть понравилось. Но в основном — нет. Окей, история про Путешествие на Запад — это классика, я всё понимаю. Но почему в Black Myth: Wukong всё так… скучно? Я, Великий Сунь Укун, должен бегать, бить демонов и слушать занудные диалоги о "судьбе" и "искуплении". Братья, я же бунтарь! Где драйв? Где хаос? Где мои 10 000 подчинённых, которые орут "УРА, КОРОЛЬ ОБЕЗЬЯН!"? Вместо этого — какая-то меланхолия и философские нравоучения. Зевает. Геймплей: "Бей, беги, повтори… и засыпай" Боссы — ладно, некоторые реально крутые (особенно те, что орут и машут здоровенными дубинами). Но большинство — просто тупые танки с кучей HP. Комбо и способности — да, я могу превращаться, делать финты и бить посохом. Но после 10-го одинакового врага хочется просто ALT+F4. Сложность — то адски сложно, то скучно легко. Баланс? Не, не слышал. И да, зачем столько катсцен? Я же обезьяна, мне надо драться, а не смотреть, как NPC 20 минут ноют о "тьме в сердце". Графика и мир: "Красиво, но пусто" Ладно, визуально игра огонь. Горы, храмы, туманы — всё как в китайской сказке. Но… где жизнь? Где толпы демонов, которые бегают и орут? Где мои весёлые приключения? Вместо этого — пустые локации и одиночество. Даже я, Великий Укун, почувствовал себя грустной мартышкой. Плюсы и минусы (по мнению уставшей обезьяны) ?? Плюсы: ?? Графика — реально красиво, прям как в легендах. ?? Некоторые боссы — вот эти да, мощные, хочется переиграть. ?? Боевка — в моменте прикольная, особенно когда разгоняешься. ?? Минусы: ? Сюжет — скучный, слишком много нытья и мало моего буйного характера. ? Повторяемость — одни и те же враги, одни и те же удары… ZZZ. ? Мир — красивый, но бездушный, как чай без сахара. ? Катсцены — слишком долгие и неинтересные. Итог: 6/10 — "Могло быть лучше, но… ладно, поиграл и хватит" Black Myth: Wukong — это как дорогой чай в красивой упаковке: выглядит круто, но на вкус — обычно. Я прошёл её чисто из упрямства, но радости мало. Если хотите настоящего Укуна — лучше перечитайте книгу. [h1] Black Myth: Wukong [/h1] This game is so much more than just another soulslike. It's imbued with chinese mythology and not just run-of-the-mill fantasy elements that you've seen a hundred times before, it has an actual skilltree that changes the way you play, armours and weapons that have an actual impact on your play style, short movies inbetween chapters that all have their own art style and most importantly an incredible amount of bosses all of which feel unique. Instead of fighting the same mob over and over and unlocking shortcuts until you reach a boss fight like in most other soulslikes [i] Black Myth: Wukong [/i] only lets you move forward for the most part and just bombards you with challenging but rewarding boss fights that will make your jaw drop. Whether you like this approach or not is up to you. There's still a lot to explore but don't expect an interconnected world with well thought out level design in the manner of [i] Dark Souls[/i]. This game stands on its own two feet.

Первые 15 минут геймплея просто привели в восторг. Всё что было дальше, задничные потуги. В общем с первым босом было сложно, но я его победил, а вот на втором забросил игру на пару месяцев. Я отчетливо понимал, что не вернусь в это дерьмо, но хотелось досмотреть историю. И я решил, что скачаю трейнеры и пройду игру до конца. В общем я так и сделал и какие выводы у меня появились: Ну игра мега красивая, стильная, как тот же bloodborn или elden ring. Но всё портит сраный жанр soul. В общем в момент прохождения с трейнером я понял, что игра эта - жуткая дрочильня. Я уставал нажимать на кнопку мыши будучи бессмертным с нескончаемой выносливостью. Единственное, что заканчивалось - собственная выносливость)) И вот ты дрочишь этих босов и начинаешь понимать, что весь этот жанр это как гавно в красивой обёртке. Весь смысл игры сводится к заучиванию тактики и оттачиванию приёмов. Игра просто пустая, я даже сюжет не совсем понял, а ведь это с учетом того, что я поставил super damage и выносил противников с 1го удара пройдя игру за 10 часов, а что было бы если бы за дрочкой в 100 часов без читов я вообще бы утерял смысл повествования!? В общем для меня жанр soul официально мертв. И я сочувствую всем тем игрокам, которые попробовали его и сломались. Не парьтесь, эти игры не оправдывают ожиданий, в них очень мало сюжетного контента и много однотипных клавонажимательств. Экономьте своё игровое время, чтобы потратить его на действительно достойные игры, такие как: ведьмак, crysis, detroit, indika, a plag tale, quantum break - игры, где старались над сюжетом, а не над текстурами и тактиками.

Black Myth: Wukong – A Revolutionary Leap into Mythic Gaming Stepping into the realm of Black Myth: Wukong is like crossing into a world where ancient legends and modern gameplay converge in a breathtaking tapestry of myth and mayhem. From its intriguing narrative roots in the classic tale of the Monkey King to its groundbreaking visuals and fluid combat, the game doesn’t just retell a story—it reinvents it for the new era of interactive storytelling. A Visual Masterpiece At first gaze, Black Myth: Wukong captures your imagination with a visual style that feels both epic and intimate. The environments evoke the delicate balance of traditional Chinese art with contemporary digital design. Each meticulously crafted scene—from the serene yet haunting landscapes to the chaotic, battle-worn temples—breathes life into the legend. The interplay of light, shadow, and hand-painted textures creates a surreal atmosphere, turning every exploration into a visual poetry performance where the past and the present entwine. Engaging Combat and Fluid Mechanics At its core, the game is powered by an energetic and dynamic combat system that marries precision with storytelling. Every battle emerges as a carefully choreographed dance, challenging you to master a variety of weaponry and mystical abilities. Combat here isn’t merely about overpowering foes; it’s about engaging in a strategic ballet where timing, reflex, and intuition determine your fate. Each enemy encounter is designed to test your mettle, ensuring that every skirmish feels both visceral and rewarding. A Deep, Resonant Narrative What truly elevates Black Myth: Wukong is its narrative depth. Inspired by the enduring legend of the Monkey King, the game dives deep into themes of rebellion, destiny, and transformation. It doesn’t just serve as a nostalgic nod to epic Chinese folklore; it reimagines these ancient tales for a modern audience, weaving in emotions and moral complexities that resonate on both personal and cultural levels. Whether you’re drawn to the myth’s iconic battles or its subtler contemplations of identity and fate, the story here feels thoughtfully crafted and strikingly relevant. Immersive Audio and Musical Score The auditory landscape of Black Myth: Wukong is as meticulously designed as its visuals. A rich and evocative musical score, blending traditional Eastern instruments with modern soundscapes, helps to amplify the game’s emotional tone. The carefully synchronized audio effects not only enhance the intensity of combat but also underscore the poignant, slower moments of discovery and reflection. Each soundbite, every note feels purposeful and crucial in knitting together an atmosphere that’s both haunting and majestic. A Bold Step Forward in Gaming Black Myth: Wukong stands as a testament to the evolving nature of narrative-driven games. It’s a bold, ambitious project that pushes the limits of what interactive experiences can be. By channeling an age-old legend into a futuristic digital canvas, it offers both longtime fans of the myth and newcomers an invitation to explore a world that is at once familiar and entirely unique. This is more than a game—it’s a bridge to cultural heritage and a celebration of artistry in motion. For gamers and storytellers alike, Black Myth: Wukong isn’t just an immersive adventure—it’s a conversation between eras, a binding of myth and technology that promises to open the door to even more reimaginings of our collective legends. What other timeless tales might be reborn in the vibrant, ever-evolving universe of digital art? The possibilities seem as infinite as the myths themselves.

No, I can’t recommend this game in good conscience, despite its UNDENIABLE strengths: PRODUCTION-WISE, THIS GAME IS ABSURDLY HIGH LEVEL. THE ANIMATIONS ARE SPECTACULAR. THE ARTISTIC WORLD IS UNBELIEVABLE. WUKONG IS A DEMO OF WHAT’S POSSIBLE IN UE5!!! A FEAST FOR GAME PHOTOGRAPHY LOVERS!!! But... that’s where the positives end. First and foremost: THIS BEAUTIFUL, MASSIVELY PRODUCED WORLD HAS THE WORST INVISIBLE WALLS I’VE EVER SEEN IN A GAME!!!!!! There’s no way to tell whether a path is blocked or leads to a secret. Getting stuck with the monkey is standard. And in a game that mimics the soulslike style, that’s a crime – it awakens frustration like nothing else. No amount of pretty visuals or graphical effects can cover up this pathetic level design. Combat in this world isn’t terrible – I actually like its simplicity – but I feel it’s too simple. Bosses didn’t pose much of a challenge, so the poor exploration design became even more painfully obvious. I won’t dwell on optimization – that’s not my area of interest. But it’s worth mentioning: it’s rough XD. In my world, though, the sheer number of unique assets and the fact that this is one of the first major titles on Unreal Engine 5 earns it some leeway in technical aspects. Still, a yellow card for the fact that without DLSS and frame generation, the game will maybe run at 5 FPS. So, does the journey in Black Myth: Wukong make any sense at all? Is there any narrative justification for this monkey’s adventure? Well... No. It’s awful. This game is exceptionally poorly written. Knowing Chinese mythology or Journey to the West isn’t an excuse, neither is targeting the Asian market. The issue lies much closer to the surface – the game tries way too hard to copy Hidetaka Miyazaki’s storytelling style, and it’s doomed from the start. His stories and storytelling methods are minimalistic, letting players interpret and discover for themselves. Wukong has a clearly defined cinematic narrative, clear goals, and straightforward interactions between characters. It’s a complete mash-up of styles – and narratively, it just doesn’t work. Because of that, the dialogues are nonsense – no line relates to the one before, characters force out emotions that neither existed earlier nor will appear later! The acts have no weight! Who cares that they’re cool, diverse, atmospheric, when there’s no connection to them! Who cares that the intro cutscenes are in different styles, if none of them have any meaning!!! They don’t complement anything, explain anything, they just stir the pot to make it all seem even more mysterious, like in FromSoft games!! It’s pathetic!!! It all gives the impression that this game only exists to be... Cool? Cool combat, cool Unreal Engine 5, cool animations, cool design, cool concept art... But no, it just doesn’t hold up. I don’t like it because I truly believed that the direction would eventually make sense. It didn’t. For the sake of being “visually stunning,” the game completely lost its narrative direction. Black Myth: Wukong is a tech demo for Unreal Engine 5 and offers little more. And that’s a shame – because as I said at the very beginning, production-wise, this game could have achieved anything. The possibilities were endless, but poor direction and narrative design crushed those dreams.

I'm so tired of souls-like games. They seem to be popping up like mushrooms on a rainy day. While this game has quite a lot of scenery and gameplay, the game looked absolutely horrible on a lower performing GPU. I had to upgrade to an RTX 5070 to disable super resolution settings for this game to look good. The environment is a constricting pipe run full of never-ending boss fights, while throughout the game you're just wondering what exactly is happening? I have no idea who these characters are, why am I interested in them, why am I fighting every creature under the sun.. The whole story is so vague and full of riddles that it's just not fun. Sure, you can treat it like any souls game where you just run and smash without even thinking what's happening around you, but it gets incredibly boring over time when every game is the same. At least tell a coherent story people can follow! It jumps all over the place and nothing is explained clearly. The changes in environment and scenery, from deserts to forests to snowy mountains is refreshing, but considering what type of hardware you need for this game to look decent and how you can't even make sense of the story, I just can't give this a thumbs up. My personal dislike for souls-like games these days also affects this review, so if you're someone who really enjoys them or hasn't really experienced them, then I'd definitely recommend Black Myth Wukong.

这是我工作几年后唯一通关的游戏。 装了些MOD——切手技优化、100%掉宝率。像给老花眼配了副眼镜，只为看清年少时错过的风景。 游戏很好。金箍棒劈开黄风岭的沙暴时，我听见了自己二十岁的心跳。可越往后走，脚步越沉。筋斗云那关，空荡荡的云雾里只剩赶路的疲惫。最终停在二郎神殿前，手柄搁在积灰的显示器旁，再没拿起来。 为何不打二周目呢。我盯着库里的《黑神话》，突然想起去年整理旧物，在老婆大学相册里看到空白页。她轻描淡写：“那时候总觉得以后有的是时间拍照。” 原以为男人的遗憾是显卡跑不动新游戏，现在才懂，是4090的光追照不进三十岁的黄昏。少年时翻墙逃课打通《仙剑》的精力，早被地铁通勤碾成粉末；曾经为隐藏BOSS反复练习的耐心，如今在短视频十五秒切换里消磨殆尽。 没打完的二郎神，像极了老婆衣柜里没拆封的旗袍。我们都在最好的年纪，误以为青春是取之不尽的点数。 ——致所有还能为游戏熬夜的年轻人： 趁教室后窗的阳光还没移走， 趁BOSS战的配乐仍在血液里燃烧。 去通关，去拍照，去失败一百次。 有些战斗，错过就是永远； 有些美丽，过期不作保存。

I initially expected this game to be a Soulslike; however, that was not the case. Though it looks like that from an outside perspective, the core mechanic of losing your currency upon dying is not present in this game. Because of that, I found the game to be more comparable to God of War. This also applies to the combat, which is very versatile and offers various different combos and playstyles, with things like armor and talismans to create builds that best suit your preferences. The graphics are beautiful, but more importantly, the art and vibe are stunning. The levels are very well designed, and it feels rewarding to explore, with things like secret bosses, loot, etc. The bosses (especially the main bosses) are really great—not too hard, but challenging enough—and the designs are unique and pretty. Overall, one of the best games I have played recently. 9.5/10

A brilliant homage to a legendary Chinese classic. Most, if not all Asians have heard of and love Journey to the West. Ask any East / Southeast Asian and we can go on and on about the beloved Monkey King Sun Wukong and his timeless escapades. As a firm root of Chinese cultural media, the story has seen various adaptations spanning decades. Black Myth: Wukong takes heavy inspiration from the original story, yet stands as its own masterful story. I was especially impressed by the well-researched, lore-accurate elements that showed up throughout the story. The effort and care put into the game are more than evident, with numerous nods to the classic lore of Journey to the West. Game Mechanics: The game’s mechanics took the gaming community by storm. I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of combat and how fluid every action was. I daresay Black Myth Wukong’s combat system is comparable to Sekiro, which I regard as the gold standard for Action RPGs. The movement and environmental barriers took some time getting used to but becomes a non-issue once you break a solid hour or two into the game. Environment/Level Design: Black Myth: Wukong’s visuals are stunning. From the perfect lighting to intricate textures and particle effects, the game’s landscapes are wallpaper-worthy in every frame. Fittingly, the game boasts neat moments for players to unwind to soft music while taking in the gorgeous scenery - a breath of fresh air amidst the fast-paced combat. The animations that take on a completely different art style throughout the game further accentuate the studio’s outstanding art direction. Enemies are also well-balanced, designed, and fit the context of each area beautifully. Again, many pay homage to the original tale while fittingly incorporating refreshing twists. Sound Design: Game Science has managed to concoct the perfect blend of traditional Chinese instruments and modern music styles. Many of the game’s soundtracks hit me hard in the gut, playing into the various in-game scenes and scenarios. As with all great games, the exquisite OSTs paired with the studio’s breathtaking world-building and level design mentioned above, creates an immersive, other-worldly atmosphere that’s hard to replicate and harder to forget. Overall, Game Science knocked my socks off with Black Myth: Wukong. At a certain point of the game, I realized we could no longer judge Black Myth: Wukong as Game Science’s first AAA game, but rather as a benchmark for what AAA games should be. The game is a love letter to both Chinese folklore and Action RPG lovers alike. The studio has me mind blown and eagerly anticipating whatever else they have in store.

Black Myth Wukong is a masterpiece. The presentation is flawlessly stunning, and the gameplay is fantastic. Despite borrowing soulslike elements and not having any blocking/ parrying (which I still find weird, my monkey has magical staffs and super strength why isn't he using his weapon to block stuff?) the game still manages to create a fluid, freeflowing combat experience that allows you to feel decently powerful as the Handsome Monkey King's reincarnation. As for the story, for someone who is familiar with the source material (I grew up reading the novel and watching the classic 1986 TV show and its sequel), I'm not exactly a fan of some of the more edgy creative choices they made (the nonsense implied romance between Wukong and the White Bone Demon, making light of the bond between Wukong and Sanzang, implying the Buddhas on mount Lingshan are bad, etc.), but overall it is an interesting interpretation that's extremely confidently presented. There are also plenty of gameplay segments/ set pieces that pay homage to the source material in clever ways which I really love. All in all Game Science absolutely knocked it out of the park with this game. Having a Journey to the West game this good is like a dream come true, and I can't wait to (hopefully) get more of this in DLCs! I will follow Game Science with great interest, as I've heard they plan to make even more Black Myth games. Maybe a fresh take on Fengshen next?

黑猴也发布快一年了，终于也是又有时间把这个国产的第一个3A大作捡起来，打通关了。 反正我玩下来的感受，就是它给个8分的评价是真的一点问题都没有。黑猴的优点和缺点都很明显。美工和引擎使用方面的技术优势带来的视觉效果绝对是顶级的，前四章虽然偶有恼怒的设计，但总的来说打的都很爽，但是到了最后两章，可能是工期的不足，让第五第六章的这两个场景完全看得出来没有用心去做，美术的参与度不高，全都是地编在干 然后到第六章花果山就更重量级了，放个地图，给你个筋斗云，你就满地图飞吧。说实话不看攻略，真的不知道要去哪打boss，触发剧情。玩到这里不由得佩服那些游戏发售初期，最初的攻略编写者，不知道他们是抱着怎样的心情，在这个完成度如同游戏demo的test ground上，让开发者像撒了几颗豆子一样随机排布了几个boss就端上来的空旷场景里四处乱逛，找寻所有能触发的boss。那几个鹿，蛤蟆，大石敢当之类的boss真给我打的一点脾气都没有，虽然最后打大圣化身，还有扭过头来打杨戬和四大天王又给我打爽了，不然冲着最后一章这个强行喂屎的游戏体验，我是真的差点就要玩不下去了。 然后说到动作系统，这个方面就能看的出来游科还是动作游戏制作的经验太少了，我是不喜欢用轮椅玩法的，我更喜欢用看破，不空和石化和boss打交互，但整个动作系统给我的感受就是，每一招每一式，它的收益和风险是不均等的，我知道黑猴是arpg，动作性上没法和act去比，但是你不能让玩家产生这么强的挫败感。就说铜头铁臂这个技能，它和聚形散气放在一个法术槽，强行二选一真的是败笔，一个boss你不打上五次，根本不知道它哪一招能打破你的石化，不是兄弟，我是天命人啊，怎么随便一个boss奋力一击就能把我从石头里打出来。不说石敢当，虎先锋，就连一个蛤蟆的石化都比我厉害，两个蓄力棍才能破掉。这个技能完全不像一个弹反类的技能该有的强度，它弹到敌人的攻击，敌人跟没事人一样，还能继续打连段，那你说我石化的意义是什么呢，用法力换棍势吗？弹反类的技能如果无法创造输出窗口，那它就不是一个合适的弹反技能。 然后是劈棍的看破，它同样没法打断敌人的攻击，以至于看破之后的二段重攻击追击变成了一个笑话，很多时候就是靠着霸体和敌人硬换血，甚至有时候敌人的攻击比较重，在空中就能把我打下来。看破的输入窗口也是，我在怪猎当太刀侠的时候，如果我预感到怪物要打过来了，我就xy反复重复短突刺和上挑，用前后摇都比较小的攻击来方便我见切躲避攻击，但放在黑猴这里，如果你想要打识破，那就只能打前两段轻击，打到第三段第四段就开始又臭又长，还没法中途打断进入重击识破的武棍花环节了。这第三第四段攻击，既没有前两段攻击的低前摇后摇，也没有最后一段轻击终结技的高伤害和高削韧，是完完全全的收益对不上风险。然后谈到派生重攻击，天赋里面那条翻滚后可以接续连段真的是如鲠在喉，你的三四段攻击做的那么又臭又长，我要识破就只能靠翻滚打断连段，重复一二段轻棍的循环，但你又加了一个翻滚后继续连招的技能，而且不是在技能数的最后，反而放在了中段，那你说我是点还是不点？我不点我就没法用后面的技能，我点了我就要翻滚之后接第三段尬舞然后挨揍。 哦对了，玩到第六章，打那几个boss明显感受到有读指令，我一出蓄力重棍就后撤步，给我当场整红温了。 还有就是有些boss，尤其是体型比较大的几个boss，被打出硬直之后，后退的距离是不是太远了点，作为积攒资源好不容易把boss打入僵直，准备一套干掉boss一大条血，最能让玩家产生多巴胺和满足感的输出窗口，让boss来个如同mhw口水硬一般的大后撤步，玩家跟不上伤害，这也太有挫败感了吧。 总的来说，这是一部瑕不掩瑜的好作品，是国产3a游戏的好的开端，它确实做到了一鸣惊人，做好了奠基者的工作，用成品回应了质疑，但确实也有很多可以改进的地方。如果要让我为这些问题找理由，那有些地方我认为是制作经验不足或者工期不足导致，有些地方我认为则是制作团队过于向美术团队倾斜，美术话语权过重，所有系统都要为视觉效果做妥协导致的。黑猴确确实实是一个标准的，优缺点都很明显，又瑕不掩瑜的八分游戏，希望dlc以及后续作品，能够在地图，动作上面继续改进，变得更强。

Black Myth Wukong is NOT a bad game. But still I wouldn't recommend it. At the start I couldn't get along with the way how Steam reviews are handled, There are no star ratings or nuances, Just a simple "yeah" or "meh". Seemed pretty unfair. But actually my opinion has changed and I'm not a big a fan of compromises either. So no, this game doesn't live up to the hype. What sucks? The gameplay. It reminds me of Witcher 3. You've got only 2 attack patterns. Light attack and heavy attack. It gets so repetitive. And frustrating because the light attack combo and the simple heavy attack are telegraphed and delayed far too long. It's not possible to interrupt yourself and enemies will exploit it. This feels sluggish like the neverending spinning attacks in Witcher 3. What else? Dodging. The gameplay consists of 90% dodging. You spend more time rolling around than actually doing something. There is no real parry, too. So you can argue that it's just the way combat works. I mean, what can a monkey with a stick achieve other than hitting hard, hitting very hard and jumping around? Yeah but look at the incredible combat styles in Ghost of Tsushima or God of War. Why it's not possible to throw your stick like a jedi? Where is my bow? If there are no shields, at least let me parry. Otherwise combat looks like this: Stun spell enemy, attack combo, dodge, dodge, dodge x100, than hit x2 enemy, dodge, dodge, dodge, wait for stun spell reset timer. The spells suck, too. There is literally just one which you always use. It's the stun. That's it. Very cheesy. So cheesy like all the bosses. Mobs are like "get out of my way". Bosses are like sponges. Unnecessary prolonged fights. Pretty unfair, too. Bosses can and will always interrupt your combos but the only way to interrupt them is to use cheesy stun spell. Sometimes bosses break out of their 100x combo suddenly and hit you hard, but it's not possible to stop your own animations.

黑神话玩完了，想说说个人体验，游戏确实不错，我全搜集了，毕竟是难得拿得出手的国产大作。 首先我得抱歉一下，魂游对我来说还是太难了，我是开了挂打的，加了一半的防御，否则连广谋那都过不去。 但是有的人说黑神话不算魂游，例如我朋友，但是STEAM商店页面明白写着魂，所以它就是，而且在我这只要是小怪伤害高大怪秒人还有存档点刷新怪的类似这些设定的游戏统统都算，马里奥也算，但是魂斗罗不算，因为魂斗罗有几条命，算变相血条。 另外，虽然普通动作游戏跟魂类不一样，但我还是要拿《暗黑血统1》这个游戏作比较，可能比较冷门而且续作一塌糊涂，所以只拿1代说，不知道这个游戏的可以云一下，也很不错，《暗黑血统1》我能做到一命通关，黑神话我可能连精英怪都打不过，这大概就是属性相克罢，但我真的很喜欢黑神话这个题材，所以哪怕开挂也玩完了。 剧情方面既然底子是西游记但跟原著出入很大，所以我就当个独立世界观看，但看表面剧情貌似就是大圣想告老还乡但上边人卸磨杀驴，然后玩家也就是天命人猴子搜集大圣遗物传承衣钵这么个事。 因为剧情里有的事情都没讲，就我个人而言的剧情猜测如下，回顾整个游戏流程和剧情，抛开游戏性和技术问题等现实因素，剧情世界中先细分成以下几个势力：西天极乐、天庭等要大圣死的势力，弥勒、杨戬、花果山等帮助猴子继承衣钵的势力。 这样才能解释为啥猴子一路搜集遗物闹出这么大动静，但敌对势力却像老式魔王勇者似的任由猴子成为新的大圣，我一开始以为是他们想培养一个听话的打手，但再看弥勒、杨戬等人的台词和剧情，我只能认为是西天或天庭出了什么幺蛾子，直接导致这些人叛离原有势力来帮猴子，简单来说是翻版的大闹天宫。 还有一些事情我暂时无法理解，例如穿越回过去时候的斯哈哩国黄风怪明显还是个护国神圣为啥后来变坏了，单看影神图，我文化水平不高，只隐隐感觉是西天有人捣鬼。 还有剧情时间中人类势力去哪了，还有那漫天神佛都去哪了之类的。 剧情说完再说说游玩时候的一些缺点，首先要说的就是地图问题，前几章给我感觉还行，绿林、荒漠、雪山，还有那些取材于真实的建筑给我看入迷了都，但是游戏中连个小地图都没有的弱引导，以及视觉疲劳是真的捞，甚至游戏整个流程涉及到例如进出室内外时候的光线过于明暗问题，开始我还以为是我我的问题，实际一搜大伙儿都这样，不过可以关掉一些设置来解决，这个就算了。 从蜘蛛洞那才是真正的黑，是真他妈黑，我上调游戏外屏幕亮度才稍微好点，再后边火焰山我开始感觉不太对劲了，就我个人而言感觉很单调，完全没有前几章的精彩。 最后的花果山才是真正的重量级，我虽然不懂游戏设计，但这个地图的功能和内容真的太捞了，那么大而空的地形靠筋斗云乱飞但跟环境几乎零交互，内容上除了主线的怪物，那四个精英怪打完啥都莫得，连个成就都没有是真难蚌，感情打完第一个搜集了图鉴就行了啊，亏我搜攻略看其他三个的位置有马不停蹄跑过去全部打完，你哪怕跟水底那个一样打完给我个成就呢， 还有那个byd大石敢当，我敢说是整个游戏最逆天最捞的BOSS，最脑瘫的秒杀机制，完全零交互的回合制，他吗的让我想到了当年玩鬼泣4大多数玩家口诛笔伐的那个巨大雕像BOSS，完了我跑去搜攻略果不其然，一堆人都吐槽这个大石敢当太过逆天，看来制作者对于这种提醒悬殊的怪物的设计把握还不够格，你哪怕弄成老战神里那种QTE呢，反正巨型BOSS也没几个吧，再不济弄成后边打二郎神那种法天象地，拳拳到肉近身搏杀撑天踏地的战斗给哥们儿真玩爽了，花果山的疲惫一扫而空，这多好啊。 但是这也算取巧，一回两回可以，多了就不行了，要么做成当年宣传片里打天兵天将，金箍棒直接变大伸长，就像杨戬用开山斧那样，打击感和世界效果不直接拉满？还能增加新鲜度，而且这游戏貌似没有格挡机制吧？感觉没有古装武打片里那种你来我往刀光剑影见招拆招的互动感，本质上还是你打你的我打我的，不过比那个byd大石敢当强太多了，那玩意儿跟DNF现在纯打桩走机制有啥区别我操。 还有感觉制作者是不是砍了一些东西，不止是这些，还有剧情，因为早期演示里准备杀白狼时候大圣本尊出来阻止了，这也是我前边说的，剧情可能是联合各方势力另一次大闹天宫，只不过早期剧情可能是大圣没死或者亲自传承衣钵这样。 反正游戏打完，冷静下来感觉制作者对于这次黑神话做的可能有些保守和赶工，再次点名批评花果山地图，给我玩吐了。

Адаптируя своего протагониста под данную игру, разработчики кажется вдохновлялись конечной интерпретацией роли Райна Рейнольдса в X-Men Origins: Wolverine, если вы понимаете о чем я ?? Интересный и вроде не слишком заезженный антураж мифов древнего Китая, где играя за каменного фурри избиваешь палкой фурри и камни... Множество боссов еще больше минибоссов, не без повторов конечно, но задушиться вроде не успел, прокачка довольно объёмная, стойки, удары с превращениями, полноценные превращения. Боевка не сложная, исключая нескольких боссов челендж скорее отсутствует. Имеются секретки, которые в принципе если внимательно играть по большей части не пропустишь, хотя кое-что, как будто больше рассчитано на рандом и без гайда не заметишь (привет крысиная стена). Сюжет в целом есть, как и общий так и отдельных локаций, несколько притчей рассказывающих о интерпретации разработчиков последствий оригинального романа, с которым я не знаком, но и без этого в принципе все понятно, будто кто-то играет в подобные игры ради сюжета. Отдельно хочется выделить анимированные ролики выполненные в разных стилях между главами, все они визуально хороши и атмосферны, а в сюжете дополняют историю локаций. Локации, вот это по мне довольно неоднозначная сторона игры, есть красивые леса и эпично выглядящие храмы, а есть невзрачно-однотонная пустыня, ну в целом это вкусовщина, но вот последняя локация это прям такое, пожертвовали красотой проработанного ландшафта ради размера локации, честно говоря это подпортило впечатление в финальной части игры. Но в целом даже со слегка смазанным впечатлением под конец, игра вышла просто прекрасной, получил больше положительных эмоций, в конце концов бить всех кого встретишь палкой это весело.

Black Myth: Wukong оставила незабываемое впечатление. До начала игры я был знаком лишь с Царем Обезьян как с персонажем китайской мифологии, но после прохождения игра пробудила во мне настоящий интерес к его полной истории и к мифологии в целом. Сюжет, на первый взгляд кажущийся запутанным, скорее, требует от игрока погружения в богатый контекст китайского фольклора. Многие персонажи и истории требуют дополнительного контекста, который можно узнать из журнала игры. Второстепенные персонажи прекрасно проработаны, их характеры чувствуются в каждом диалоге и действии. Левел-дизайн, хоть и имеет элементы коридорности, тем не менее предоставляет достаточно пространства для исследования. Каждая локация уникальна и манит своей красотой и секретами, я с огромным удовольствием изучал каждый уголок, закрыв все секретные локации. Боевая система, построенная вокруг посоха (или копья с отличиями в анимации атаки), оказалась на удивление увлекательной. Несмотря на кажущуюся однотипность оружия, динамичный темп боя и разнообразие способностей не дают заскучать. Прогрессия в игре ощущается очень хорошо – чувствуется, как с каждым этапом сюжета ты становишься сильнее, а исследование локаций отражает этот прогресс на броне и оружии. Графика и оптимизация находятся на высоком уровне. Иногда встречал микрофризы, особенно в насыщенных эффектами сценах, но это несущественно. В целом, Black Myth: Wukong затянула меня на 40 часов полного исследования игры, и после финальных титров мне совершенно не хотелось покидать этот удивительный мир. Black Myth: Wukong – не просто времяпровождение, это незабываемое приключение, которое хочется пережить заново.

When this game first came out, I wasn't sure about it. This one was a slow burn for me. Taking months after purchase to get in to. But once I hit that critical 10-15 hour milestone... oh my goodness did this game open up. I am constantly in awe of this game, the environments are just so breathtaking. But all of that isn't worth it if the gameplay isn't there, and this game has it in abundance. The combat, the progression, the abilities, the enemy variety... I mean it's all just a freaking blast. At first I was annoyed by the invisible walls, but I kind of started to accept it as it keeps the experience very focused, and it allowed you to take in the majestic views of the landscape without dying from a big ass bottomless mountain jump. I am really impressed with this game. Now, you probably need to be familiar with the difficulty of games like Dark Souls, Elden Ring, Lies of P, Sekiro, and the "souls" genre in general. But where this game softens it up a little bit is you don't drop your experience points and need to pick them up again to progress, you just keep your experience. Now, don't get me wrong, the game has some brutal fights that will test your patience.... but you still get that same dopamine hit after persevering and defeating a crazy strong foe. My advice is don't give up at the White Clad Noble... keep pushing through. The game opens up and you will be rewarded with some of the most magnificent level design you have ever seen. I am super impressed with this game, you should give it a chance!

[b]可能有剧透：[/b] 我是手残、996上班族，此前玩过的最吃操作的3D动作游戏是旷野之息。去年8月一边兴奋一边担忧着入了手，开始的时候我完全不看攻略和剧透，只想自己摸索（大数据推送我都直接划走）。但不幸的是我这次打着打着又变成了一名仓鼠玩家，早期没有小地图，我为了探图反反复复迷过路（甚至时隔多年又晕了3D），我为了打boss拼命刷小怪，我细细地读过每件物品每件兵器披挂的描述、品味过影神图里的每篇聊斋小短文，我与所见之物都尽量进行了互动。就这样断断续续磕磕绊绊打了4、50个小时，硬是打到第四章，直到百眼魔君那里二阶段死活打过不去，万念俱灰弃游了几个月。 后来跟朋友聊天，说是百眼魔君要用绣花针，才发现我都打到第四章了法宝还只有一个避火罩，就感觉我玩的和别人玩的是两个游戏。于是我从这里开始，头一次学习了轮椅打法，头一次看了网上的攻略，回到第二章拿了定风珠（没错我在这时才明白“我来助你”的梗图是从哪来的）、回到第三章拿了禁字诀（没错我在这之前总想着用火系技能给老头暖身子）、回到第四章终于打过了晦月魔君拿到了绣花针。之后不看攻略一路还算顺利地莽到了大圣面前（因为之前刷级，后面就一路砍瓜切菜）。直到重来十几次还被大圣反复橄榄，再再一次学习了轮椅打法，成功打出BE。想起剧透还有二郎神，于是再查漏补缺（顺便发现至少漏了四只龙，不知道还漏了什么没有）。回到第三章又反复被二郎神橄榄几次，再再再一次学习了轮椅打法，最终打出GE，此时游戏时长也来到了85小时，终于，在2025年6月8日（高考第二天），我打过了一周目，成就63/81。 敲了这么多字儿我不是想吐槽游戏的地图设计和引导（毕竟现在看已经有很多人吐槽过了），我只是想把我的游玩过程跟大家分享一波。我能感受到游科成员对这个游戏的爱和投入，因为他们干了很多只有强迫症才会干的事情。 打出GE后有种五味杂陈的感觉，既有剧情给我的感动（太浪漫了），也有对自己没能一次就获得最佳的游戏体验的遗憾，也有发现自己其实只要看攻略就能节省很多时间的无奈。不管怎样，山就在那里，而我已经站在了其中一座的山顶了。 刚才突然想查一下有没有人讨论过不看攻略的可能性，还真让我找到一个帖子。我不知道我的这个评论会有多少人看到，也许在全国全世界的评论的汪洋大海中，我的这一滴小小浪花不会有人看到，不过也没有关系，传送门：https://tieba.baidu.com/p/9147429103

怎麼說呢, 從幾年前黑神話預告時, 就很密切注意這個遊戲. 玩完一周目後, 一切都很好; 場景、音樂、故事、操作、道具..., 怕以後很難超越了. 我說一下可以改進的地方, 3D 遊戲的通病, 就是戰鬥視角, 鎖定敵人後, 敵人亂飛亂跳, 或是跑到場景的死角, 玩家都看不到自己或者敵人的蹤影. 這點提個建議, 若偵測到看不到自己或敵人時, 特別是自己, 應該可以讓視角切到 正對玩家的45度角俯視, 或者乾脆把遮住玩家的場景變透明. 另外, 當我們視角看不到敵人, 而敵人就在我們周圍時, 即便看不到敵人的時候, 按鎖定也應該要應鎖定敵人. 還有一點, 人物轉身時, 一般視角都還是在原地, 建議按鎖定, 可以快把視角切到人物面對的那個方向. 就有點像視角定位. 這個功能在太空戰士(仁王或其它3D動作都有, 我想悟空應該是漏加了而己.) 期望出修正, 或DLC或續作. 一定支持.
